name: Evaporitic Karst and Caves of Northern Apennines
description: In northern Italy's Emilia-Romagna region, this group of protected areas preserves a landscape of gypsum rock riddled with more than 900 caves, which together stretch over 100 kilometres underground. Some of them plunge 265 metres down, among the deepest gypsum caves anywhere. Scholars have studied this terrain since the 16th century, making it the world's first evaporitic karst to be explored scientifically.
